name: Checkbox group
summary: Lets people pick any number of options from a short, visible set, under one legend.
description: A checkbox group shows every option at once, with a legend naming the choice, and lets people check any number of them, including none. It is the grouped form of the Checkbox: the group carries the legend, the shared help text and the error message, and each option its own label, description, value and checked state. Exactly one choice is a Radio group; a long list is a Select.

anatomy.description: Root: the group of options (a fieldset on the web). Carries the orientation, the size and the states forced for review.
Text naming the choice. Provides the group's accessible name.
Optional help text under the legend, associated with every option as its description.
One option: its checkbox, label and description on a grid. Takes the states of the control it holds.

properties.name: Label
properties.description: Name of the option. Provides the radio's accessible name.

properties.name: Value
properties.description: Value submitted when the option is checked. Defaults to the option's position.

properties.name: Description
properties.description: Help text under the option's label, exposed as the radio's description.

properties.name: Checked
properties.description: Whether this option is on. Any number of options may be checked.

properties.name: Disabled
properties.description: The option stays visible, dimmed, and cannot be chosen.

anatomy.description: The box of the option: the native checkbox, drawn by the component as the Checkbox's. Receives focus, holds the checked state and shows it with a check mark.
Text naming the option; activating it toggles the box.
Optional help text under the option's label.
Text saying what is wrong and what to do, associated with every option as a description. Shown only with a severity.

options.description: One option per line, the default: easiest to scan and leaves room for descriptions.
Options on one line, wrapping when needed: two or three short options (Yes / No).

properties.name: Size
properties.description: Box size, option label and description text size scale together; the legend, the description and the message take the field family's sizes per size (Forms rule anatomy).

properties.name: Legend
properties.description: The question or the set of options (Notifications).

properties.name: Description
properties.description: Help text for the whole choice.

properties.name: Name
properties.description: Form field name shared by every option (each checked option submits its value under it). Defaults to the group's id.

properties.name: Message
properties.description: What is wrong and what to do, shown with a severity. Replaces errorMessage.

properties.name: Required
properties.description: At least one option must be checked. No box carries the native requirement, which would require that very box; the product checks the group when the form is submitted and says so in the message (Choose at least one).

properties.name: Severity
properties.description: What the check of the value found. A choice has nothing to confirm or to warn about, so only error exists (decision forms-severity).

options.description: Validation failed on the group: every box takes the error border, the message says what to do and every option is exposed as in error (aria-invalid on the web).

properties.name: Disabled
properties.description: Disables the whole group; the chosen option stays visible.

states.description: Resting, unchecked: an outlined empty box.
Pointer over a box or its label. The empty box takes a light tint; a checked box does not change. Needs a pointing device: touch has no hover.
Keyboard focus on a radio. Shows the shared focus ring outside it; pointer focus shows none.
A checked option (the entry's checked property): the box fills with the brand color and shows a check mark.
Severity error on the group: every box border takes the error color, every unchecked box the subtle error fill (a checked box keeps its brand fill), and the message is shown.
Non-interactive, for the whole group or for one option: box, label and description drop to the shared disabled colors.

notes: The legend comes first, the description right under it (no gap: the two read as one heading), then the options and the message, separated by container.row-gap; on the web the legend's bottom margin carries that gap when no description follows, since a rendered legend sits outside its fieldset's flow.
Options stack vertically, or flow on one line and wrap in the horizontal orientation, separated by container.gap for the orientation.
Within an option, the box sits before the label, centered on its first line; the option's description sits under its label.

name.text: The group is named by its legend (the fieldset's first legend element on the web). Each option is named by its own label, associated as its label element; descriptions and the message are exposed as descriptions of the checkboxes, not as part of their names.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to each enabled option in turn: unlike radios, every checkbox is a tab stop. Disabled options are skipped.
Checks or unchecks the focused option.

guidelines.text: Expose the group, its name, each option's name and checked state through the platform's native checkboxes and grouping, so assistive technology receives them without extra work.

Use native input type=checkbox elements inside a fieldset whose legend names the set: the fieldset exposes the group role and its name, each checkbox its role and checked state. Never add aria-checked to a native checkbox.
Help text and the message are referenced by aria-describedby from every box, so they are read as descriptions after an option's name.
Never rely on color alone: each checked option is shown by its check mark, an error is stated in text, not only by the red borders.

Legend, option labels and descriptions contrast at least 4.5:1 with the surface in every color mode and enabled state: 19.03:1 (primary text) and 12.78:1 (descriptions) in light mode, 11.28:1 and 8.86:1 in dark mode on the default surface; the error message 6.12:1 (light) and 7.06:1 (dark). Disabled text is inactive and exempt.

Each box is what identifies its option and shows its state, so its border, its fill and its dot contrast at least 3:1 with adjacent colors in every color mode: unchecked border 12.78:1 (light) and 11.28:1 (dark) on the default surface; checked fill 5.77:1 and 12.76:1; the dot on the fill 5.72:1 and 13.05:1; the error border (the accent functional border) 6.12:1 and 4.97:1, at least 5.79:1 and 3.73:1 on every surface level; the focus ring 5.77:1 and 12.76:1. Disabled is exempt.
A visible focus indicator appears on the focused box, drawn outside it.
The focus ring is drawn with :focus-visible, so pointer focus shows no ring.

A box alone is 16 or 20 CSS pixels, under the 24 pixel minimum; its label is part of the target and brings the option above it, and the spacing exception applies when options are 24 pixels apart: medium options are 24 pixels tall, 28 pixels from one to the next, and small ones 21 pixels tall, 25 pixels apart, so their 24 pixel circles clear each other by 1 pixel.

When no option is chosen in a required group, say so with aria-invalid on the boxes and describe the error in text (Choose at least one). No box carries the required attribute: on a checkbox it requires that very box, so the browser would ask for one given option, or for every option, never for one of several; the product checks the group when the form is submitted.

A required group's "(required)" stays in its legend's text, so it is part of the group's name: no state says that a group is required, since aria-required is not supported on the group role a fieldset maps to.
A set of consents that must all be accepted is not a required group: each consent is a separate required Checkbox, which the platform requires checked.

Disabling the group with the fieldset's disabled attribute disables every box and removes them from the focus order; a disabled option uses its own disabled attribute. When people need to know an option exists, keep it enabled and explain.

Apple recommends a hit region of at least 44 x 44 pt; each option (box and label) must reach it on iOS. Options 4 pt apart cannot share the space between them as a field's hit region does, so each option row is at least 44 pt tall, its box and label centred in it, with 4 pt between rows; the legend, the description and the message keep their 0 and 6 pt and grow with Dynamic Type. Avoid relying solely on different colors to communicate the state.

Android recommends a touch target of at least 48 x 48 dp; Material's Checkbox sets that minimum itself when it can receive actions, so each option row is at least 48 dp tall, 4 dp apart. Lift the selection to the row with the toggleable modifier and the Checkbox role, so label and radio form one element whose state is announced.
On macOS, Apple's minimum control size is 20 x 20 pt (28 x 28 pt by default): an option row, 21 pt small and 24 pt medium, meets the minimum, so the options keep the default spacing, 4 pt apart.
Color transitions of the boxes are removed when the user asks for reduced motion.

guidelines: The legend names the set of options: Notifications, Toppings, Which days suit you?
Option labels are short, parallel and positive: Email, Push, Text message. Sentence case, no trailing punctuation.
Put consequences in an option's description, not in its label.
Say when a choice is required or limited in the description: Choose at least one; Choose up to three.
The message of an error says what to do, relying on the legend it sits under: Choose at least one

decisions.text: The legend, the description and the message take the field family's text sizes per size (small and medium): the legend 14 / 16 px (medium, tight line height), the description 12 / 12 px, the message 14 / 16 px (medium). Before, all three were 14 px at every size. Option labels and option descriptions keep their sizes. A default, which this component's own refinement may revisit.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-26 (#105 step 2b, point b4, option A as recommended); it follows the Forms foundation's decision forms-text-sizes. The team's words: "We choose A but we'll probably refine them properly when we'll tackle the Select, Checkbox Group, etc. form controls."

decisions.text: Every unchecked box in error takes the subtle error fill (control.background.error = global.bg.subtle.functional.error.default) inside its error border, at rest and on hover alike; a checked box keeps its brand fill, so checked still reads checked. On hover an empty box in error keeps its fill and its error border (before, hover turned its border back to the neutral one).
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-26 (#105 step 2b, point b3, option B chosen over the recommended A, border only); it follows the Forms foundation's decision forms-choice-error-fill, where the options and their reasons are recorded. Measured: The error border on the fill 5.45:1 in light mode and 5.14:1 in dark mode (WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1), on the surface levels 0 to 3 unchanged (6.12 / 5.79 / 6.12 / 5.79:1 light, 4.97 / 4.55 / 4.16 / 3.73:1 dark); the fill against the surface 1.12 / 1.06 / 1.12 / 1.06:1 light and 1.03 / 1.12 / 1.23 / 1.37:1 dark, decoration, not the cue.

decisions.text: A required Checkbox group means at least one option checked. No box carries the required attribute (before, the first box did, so the browser blocked the submit until that one option was checked, even when another was); the product checks the group when the form is submitted and its message says "Choose at least one". On the web the legend's "(required)" stays in the group's name, since no state says that a group is required. Consents that must all be accepted are separate required Checkboxes.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-26 (#105 step 2b, point b2, option A as recommended); it follows the Forms foundation's decision forms-required-group, where the options and their reasons are recorded. Sources opened on 2026-11-27: WAI-ARIA 1.2 aria-required, HTML Checkbox state, HTML-AAM fieldset.

decisions.text: The group's parts are 6 px apart (container.row-gap = space.6): the legend to the options when there is no description, the description to the options, the options to the message. The description sits right under its legend (0 px): the two read as one heading. Options stack vertically 4 px apart (container.gap.vertical = space.4), closer than the parts around them, so the list reads as one unit; the horizontal orientation keeps one wrapping line, 16 px apart. The values are the same on every platform; on iOS and Android each option row grows to the platform's minimum target and keeps the 4 pt or dp between rows. Before, the parts were 8 px apart, the options 8 px, and the legend touched its next part (0 px), as the gap never reached a rendered legend.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-26 (#105 step 10, point 5, option D, proposed by the team, its three assumed values confirmed: "Yes, D as assumed, and deduce what's expected for the other platforms"). It follows the Forms foundation's decision forms-part-gaps. Rejected: today's values (8 between parts and options, the legend at 0 to everything: a bug, the legend + * rule cancelling the margin its comment promised), A (6 everywhere, options 8 apart), B (fields 6, groups 8), C (8 everywhere, reopening the Text field's 6). Measured on the web: medium options 24 px tall, 28 px from one to the next; small options 21 px tall, 25 px apart, so the 24 px circles of WCAG 2.5.8's spacing exception clear each other by 1 px.

decisions.text: The group shows the error severity, set by the severity property (none by default, error): every box takes the accent functional error border color and the message, shown only with a severity, takes the error text color. Warning and success do not exist for a group of choices: that is our judgment, not a source's. Severity replaces the invalid property and message replaces errorMessage. On the web the error is aria-invalid="true" on every option and data-severity on the root. The accent error border reaches 3:1 on every surface level since the Color foundation 7.1.0 (decision border-accent-functional-3-to-1).
decisions.rationale: The team validated the Forms foundation's three severities (decision forms-validation-severities) and named the property severity; "error" is the word every platform uses (WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, Compose error semantics, Material error text), where "invalid" is the web's technical term. The clean break is deliberate: the packages are alpha and unreleased, and a deprecated alias would cost a schema field and support in the validator, the bridge and the templates. This amends decisions field-colors and label-description-error, whose text still says invalid and error message.

decisions.text: The component is the whole group: a legend, optional help text, the options as a repeated part (label, value, description, checked, disabled) and an error message, on the model of the Radio group. On the web it is a fieldset of native checkboxes sharing one name; a single option stays the Checkbox.
The boxes follow the Checkbox's selection control colors.
Options stack vertically by default, 8 px apart; the horizontal orientation puts them on one wrapping line, 16 px apart, as the Radio group.
Two sizes as the Checkbox: small (16 px box, 2 px corners, 14 px label) and medium (20 px box, 4 px corners, 16 px label, the default); the box border is 1.2 px.

changelog.note: Forms decision forms-guidelines-once (#105 step 2b, point b5): the form-wide guidelines leave this specification, said once in the Forms foundation and listed on this page under "From the Forms foundation", by the tiers this control follows: the legend and option labels guideline. The references only they cited are dropped. No rendering change.

Decision text-sizes (Forms forms-text-sizes, #105 step 2b, point b4): legend.typography, description.typography and message.typography become one token per size (small and medium): the legend 14 / 16 px (medium, tight line height), the description 12 / 12 px, the message 14 / 16 px (medium), all 14 px before; the size property now affects these parts. No color change.

Decision error-fill (Forms forms-choice-error-fill, #105 step 2b, point b3): new token control.background.error → global.bg.subtle.functional.error.default, every unchecked box in error filled with it inside its error border, a checked box keeps its brand fill. The error border on the fill 5.45:1 in light mode and 5.14:1 in dark mode (WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1), on the surface levels 0 to 3 unchanged (6.12 / 5.79 / 6.12 / 5.79:1 light, 4.97 / 4.55 / 4.16 / 3.73:1 dark); the fill against the surface 1.12 / 1.06 / 1.12 / 1.06:1 light and 1.03 / 1.12 / 1.23 / 1.37:1 dark, decoration, not the cue. On hover an empty box in error keeps its fill and its error border (before, hover turned its border back to the neutral one).

Decision required-at-least-one (Forms forms-required-group, #105 step 2b, point b2): the template no longer puts required on the first box (the browser asked for that one option, a bug); the required property means at least one option, checked by the product. The required-group guideline is rewritten and two guidelines are added: the legend's "(required)" stays in the name on the web, consents are separate Checkboxes; the WAI validation tutorial, cited only for the required attribute, is dropped. No token or rendering change.

Decision part-gaps (supersedes orientations; Forms forms-part-gaps, #105 step 10, point 5): container.row-gap space.8 → space.6 and container.gap.vertical space.8 → space.4; the legend's bottom margin takes the row gap (the legend touched its next part before, 0 px: fixed), 0 when the description follows it. The layout note, the iOS, Android and 2.5.8 guidelines and a new macOS guideline say the platform rows: iOS rows at least 44 pt, Android 48 dp, both 4 apart; macOS meets its 20 pt minimum. Measured: medium options 24 px tall, 28 apart; small 21, 25 apart (2.5.8 spacing exception by 1 px). The Figma blueprint draws the legend and the description in a heading frame with no gap. No color change.

Fix: the example's error message and the content guideline rely on the label it sits under and no longer repeat the field's name ("Choose at least one"), as the Forms foundation decides (forms-message-relies-on-label). No rendering change.
Fix: the examples' message and description of one sentence end with no period, as the Forms foundation decides (forms-message-punctuation). No rendering change.

Breaking, decision forms-severity: the invalid property is replaced by severity (none, error), errorMessage by message and the part error-message by message, the state invalid by error; the web attribute data-invalid by data-severity. Tokens: control.border-color.invalid is control.border-color.error and reads the accent functional border (global.border.accent.functional.<severity>.default) instead of the base error border; error-message.* is message.*, and message.color.<severity> reads global.text.on-base.functional.<severity>.default. CSS: [data-severity="<severity>"] and [data-state="<severity>"], checkbox-group__error-message is checkbox-group__message. The accent error border reaches 3:1 on every surface level since the Color foundation 7.1.0 (decision border-accent-functional-3-to-1).

Fix, no decision changed: the Figma library's POC2 export (Color foundation 3.1.0) moves the values of the roles the tokens alias; the tokens, CSS and template are unchanged. Light: 9 tokens follow the ash retune (one to four units per channel); error-message.color reads global.text.on-base.functional.error.default: #E12A23 becomes #C01619. Dark: 9 tokens follow the ash retune (one to four units per channel); error-message.color reads global.text.on-base.functional.error.default: #EE5248 becomes #F88275; control.border-color.default, control.border-color.hover reads global.border.accent.neutral.default: #B9B7B7 becomes #CFCFCF; control.border-color.invalid reads global.border.base.functional.error.default: #E12A23 becomes #DF2821. Contrast re-measured on the accessibility guidelines: 3.82 → 3.73:1, 4.52 → 6.12:1, 4.97 → 7.06:1, 5.74 → 5.72:1, 5.79 → 5.77:1, 11.27 → 11.28:1, 12.80 → 12.76:1, 12.87 → 12.78:1, 13.04 → 13.05:1, 19.07 → 19.03:1.

Initial draft (decisions group-of-native-checkboxes, selection-control-colors, orientations, sizes). Fieldset of native checkboxes with legend, description, option descriptions and error message; states default, hover, focus-visible, checked, invalid, disabled on the option part; orientations vertical and horizontal; sizes small and medium. Contrast as the Checkbox and the Radio group (light / dark, default surface): labels 19.07 / 11.27, descriptions 12.87 / 8.80, error text 4.52 / 4.97, unchecked border 12.87 / 8.80, checked fill 5.79 / 12.80, mark 5.74 / 13.04, error border 6.12 / 3.82, focus ring 5.79 / 12.80.
